record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For bipartite Gaussian quantum states, entanglement of formation is defined by minimizing the average pure-state entanglement over all convex decompositions. For certain two-mode Gaussian states this minimum can be achieved using decompositions into pure Gaussian states that are translates of one squeezed Gaussian state with Gaussian weights. Is this true for all Gaussian states, equivalently does Gaussian entanglement of formation equal ordinary entanglement of formation for every Gaussian state?

evidence.quote: Entanglement of formation is defined as a minimimum over all convex decompositions of a bipartite state into pure states (see problem 7). It has been shown for certain two-mode Gaussian states this minimum can be taken over decompositions of the given state into pure states, all of which are translates of the same squeezed Gaussian state, with Gaussian weights.
Show (or disprove) that this is true for all Gaussian states.
With this, the above question reads: Does Gaussian entanglement of formation equal entanglement of formation for all Gaussian states?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a bipartite continuous-variable quantum system with Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$ where $\mathcal{H}_A=L^2(\mathbb{R}^m)$ and $\mathcal{H}_B=L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$. A Gaussian state $\rho$ on this system is a density operator whose Wigner function is a Gaussian on phase space $\mathbb{R}^{2(m+n)}$; equivalently, its characteristic function $\chi_\rho(\xi)=\mathrm{tr}(\rho\, W(\xi))$ is a Gaussian, where $W(\xi)$ are the Weyl displacement operators.

Entanglement of formation. For any bipartite mixed state $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$, the entanglement of formation is
$$E_F(\rho)=\inf\Big\{\sum_i p_i\, S\!\big(\mathrm{tr}_B|\psi_i\rangle\langle\psi_i|\big)\;:\;\rho=\sum_i p_i|\psi_i\rangle\langle\psi_i|,\ p_i\geq 0,\ \sum_i p_i=1\Big\},$$
where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$ is the von Neumann entropy and the infimum is over all convex decompositions of $\rho$ into pure states (allowing continuous decompositions $\rho=\int |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\,d\mu(\psi)$).

Gaussian entanglement of formation. The Gaussian entanglement of formation $E_F^G(\rho)$ is defined for a Gaussian state $\rho$ by restricting the infimum above to convex decompositions in which every pure state $|\psi_i\rangle$ is a pure Gaussian state. Equivalently, one may restrict to decompositions of the form
$$\rho=\int W(\xi)|\psi_0\rangle\langle\psi_0| W(\xi)^*\, g(\xi)\, d\xi,$$
where $|\psi_0\rangle$ is a fixed pure Gaussian (squeezed) state and $g$ is a Gaussian probability density on phase space.

Question. Prove or disprove: for every bipartite Gaussian state $\rho$,
$$E_F^G(\rho)=E_F(\rho).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been established for all two-mode Gaussian states (Akbari-Kourbolagh & Akhound and prior work, removing earlier symmetry assumptions). For general multi-mode Gaussian states the equality of Gaussian entanglement of formation with ordinary entanglement of formation remains open, as recorded on the IQOQI Open Quantum Problems list.

status_evidence.snippet: Optimal Gaussian decomposition shown to give the entanglement of formation for arbitrary two-mode Gaussian states.

status_evidence.title: Quantifying entanglement of formation for two-mode Gaussian states
status_evidence.snippet: Provides bounds and numerical estimation of entanglement of formation for two-mode Gaussian states, indicating the multi-mode question remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research focuses on bounds, with the general multi-mode question still open.
